chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: We are in the mountain, and we send the shepherds to the sheep. Sometimes a sheep is injured or something happens to it, and they slaughter it; then may we eat it?
He عليه السلام said: No. It is only a matter of slaughtered meat, and none may be trusted concerning it except a Muslim.

key_terms.الذَّبِيحَةُ: the slaughtered animal whose permissibility depends on valid slaughter
key_terms.الرُّعَاةَ: the shepherds sent to tend the flock
key_terms.الْغَنَمِ: the sheep or flock being grazed
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُ: the Muslim, whose slaughter is trusted in this ruling
key_terms.عَطِبَتِ: became injured, damaged, or near destruction

ai.seo_question: Can meat slaughtered by non-Muslim shepherds be eaten in Shiʿi fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on eating an animal slaughtered by shepherds when the owners are absent. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that such slaughter is not relied upon unless performed by a Muslim, indicating the requirement of a trustworthy Muslim slaughterer in matters of dhabīḥah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4184 - Al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah (swt) who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (as), "We are in the mountains and we send the shepherds to the sheep. Sometimes a sheep is injured or something happens to it, and they slaughter it. Can we eat it?"
Imam (as) said: "No, for it is a matter of proper slaughtering, and only a Muslim can be trusted with it."
